title: Andor
because: Rogue One, Slow Horses, The Americans
why: A grounded spy thriller set in the Star Wars universe, with almost no Jedi and a lot of slow-burn tension.

title: The Last of Us
because: The Walking Dead, Fallout, Silo
why: Post-apocalyptic drama that cares more about the people than the monsters.

title: Shōgun
because: Marco Polo, Age of Samurai, The Pillars of the Earth
why: Political intrigue in feudal Japan, told largely in Japanese and beautifully made.

title: Succession
because: House of Cards, Ozark, Better Call Saul
why: A media dynasty tearing itself apart; vicious, funny and very well acted.

title: Fargo
because: Breaking Bad, Ozark, Better Call Saul
why: An anthology of crime stories where ordinary people make terrible choices.

title: Counterpart
because: Fringe, Dark Matter, Severance
why: Cold-war spy story with a parallel world and two versions of every character.

title: Devs
because: Ex Machina, Severance, Mr. Robot
why: Alex Garland's miniseries about a tech company with a secret quantum project.

title: Halt and Catch Fire
because: Mr. Robot, The IT Crowd, Silk Road
why: The 80s and 90s PC and internet boom through the people who built it.

title: The Leftovers
because: Lost, The OA, Fringe
why: Life after 2% of the world vanishes; strange, emotional and unlike anything else.

title: Battlestar Galactica
because: The Expanse, For All Mankind, Firefly
why: Military sci-fi with real politics and moral dilemmas; still one of the best.

title: Paradise
because: Silo, Designated Survivor, Pluribus
why: A presidential murder in a very unusual town, with twists you won't see coming.

title: The Diplomat
because: Homeland, House of Cards, Designated Survivor
why: Fast, witty foreign-policy thriller about a reluctant ambassador.

title: Barry
because: Better Call Saul, Arrested Development, Breaking Bad
why: A hitman who wants to be an actor; a comedy that gets very dark.

title: Peep Show
because: The IT Crowd, The Office, Arrested Development
why: Cringe comedy told from inside two flatmates' heads.

title: Arrival
because: Contact, Her, Ex Machina
why: First-contact story about language and time, closer to Contact than to an action movie.

title: Interstellar
because: Contact, Tenet, Apollo 13
why: Nolan's space epic about time, gravity and family.

title: Blade Runner 2049
because: Blade Runner, Ex Machina, Gattaca
why: A worthy sequel; slow, gorgeous and thoughtful.

title: Annihilation
because: Ex Machina, Moon, The Girl with All the Gifts
why: Alex Garland's eerie sci-fi about an expedition into a zone where nature mutates.

title: Coherence
because: Cube, Dark Matter, Dark
why: A dinner party during a comet goes wrong in mind-bending ways, made on a tiny budget.

title: Rush
because: Senna
why: Hunt vs. Lauda's 1976 Formula 1 rivalry; a natural follow-up to Senna.

title: This Is Spinal Tap
because: Rush: Beyond the Lighted Stage, Tenacious D, The Dirt
why: The original rock mockumentary, essential for anyone who has been in a band.

title: Zodiac
because: Mindhunter, Making a Murderer, Dexter
why: Fincher's obsessive, true-crime hunt for the Zodiac killer.

title: Sicario
because: Narcos, Breaking Bad, No Country for Old Men
why: Tense, brutal look at the war on cartels at the US-Mexico border.

title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
because: Snatch, Pulp Fiction
why: Guy Ritchie's first, and the blueprint for Snatch.

title: Hot Fuzz
because: Tropic Thunder, What We Do in the Shadows, Anchorman
why: A buddy-cop parody that keeps getting funnier on rewatch.

title: Palm Springs
because: Groundhog Day, About Time, Yes Man
why: A time-loop romantic comedy that finds new things to do with the idea.

title: The Prestige
because: Tenet, The Usual Suspects, Memento
why: Two rival magicians; a Nolan puzzle with a great final reveal.

title: Source Code
because: Edge of Tomorrow, Déjà Vu, Groundhog Day
why: A soldier relives the same eight minutes on a train to find a bomber.
